problem_statement: RISC-V PMP must support custom, user-defined memory protection regions declared in the Device Tree via the zephyr,memory-attr property. When such regions are defined (with CONFIG_MEM_ATTR enabled), the PMP must program entries that cover each DT-defined region with the requested read/write/execute permissions, and the resulting PMP address and configuration registers must reflect those regions. The initial mstatus must also reflect a valid machine-mode PMP configuration (MPRV enabled, MPP not left in M-mode before user-mode entry). This includes converting the DT memory-attribute flags into the correct PMP permission bits (R/W/X).

verification.reason: The hidden tests call three specific public symbols (DT_MEM_RISCV_TO_PMP_PERM, pmp_decode_region, z_riscv_pmp_read_config, z_riscv_pmp_read_addr) by name, and rely on them being non-static under CONFIG_ZTEST; the statement describes the behaviour but omits every exact name and the accessibility requirement, all of which can be added without dictating implementation.

problems.detail: The test calls the macro DT_MEM_RISCV_TO_PMP_PERM directly, but the statement only describes the conversion behaviour without giving the macro's exact name.

The test calls pmp_decode_region(cfg_byte, pmp_addr, index, &start, &end) directly, but the statement never mentions this function, its signature, or its behaviour (decoding TOR, NA4, NAPOT PMP entries into start/end addresses).

The test calls z_riscv_pmp_read_config and z_riscv_pmp_read_addr directly. The statement never mentions these function names or that they must be made accessible (non-static) when CONFIG_ZTEST is defined.

The test relies on z_riscv_pmp_read_config, z_riscv_pmp_read_addr, and pmp_decode_region being callable from test code (non-static under CONFIG_ZTEST), but the statement does not state this interface property.

problem_statement_fixed: RISC-V PMP must support custom, user-defined memory protection regions declared in the Device Tree via the zephyr,memory-attr property. When such regions are defined (with CONFIG_MEM_ATTR enabled), the PMP must program entries that cover each DT-defined region with the requested read/write/execute permissions, and the resulting PMP address and configuration registers must reflect those regions. The initial mstatus must also reflect a valid machine-mode PMP configuration (MPRV enabled, MPP not left in M-mode before user-mode entry). This includes converting the DT memory-attribute flags into the correct PMP permission bits (R/W/X) via a macro named DT_MEM_RISCV_TO_PMP_PERM that maps DT_MEM_RISCV_TYPE_IO_R to PMP_R, DT_MEM_RISCV_TYPE_IO_W to PMP_W, DT_MEM_RISCV_TYPE_IO_X to PMP_X, and returns 0 for DT_MEM_RISCV_TYPE_EMPTY or a zero input. A function pmp_decode_region(uint8_t cfg_byte, unsigned long *pmp_addr, unsigned int index, unsigned long *start, unsigned long *end) must be available to decode a PMP configuration byte and the corresponding entry from the address register array into start and end addresses. The functions z_riscv_pmp_read_config(unsigned long *pmp_cfg, size_t pmp_cfg_size) and z_riscv_pmp_read_addr(unsigned long *pmp_addr, size_t pmp_addr_size) must be accessible (non-static) when CONFIG_ZTEST is defined, so that external code can read the current PMP configuration and address register contents.
